evals.prompt: Set up my vault -- I want to start using the memory vault pattern for the first time.
evals.expected_behavior: Runs vault-init. Loads vault-conventions first, proposes ~/memory-vault (never a project repo path), checks the target does not already contain INDEX.md before proceeding, then builds the full structure, seeds 3-5 facts elicited from the user with honest provenance, writes the first episode, and hands over the verbatim Cowork/Claude Code setup lines.

evals.prompt: Initialize the memory vault for me.
evals.expected_behavior: Runs vault-init. Matches the description's listed trigger phrase directly. Refuses to double-init if INDEX.md already exists at the target, offering to inspect instead of overwriting.

evals.prompt: Capture this session to the vault -- oh, and I don't actually have a vault set up yet.
evals.expected_behavior: Does not silently run vault-init on its own initiative. disable-model-invocation means this skill only runs when the user explicitly asks for it -- per vault-capture's own step 1, the correct move is to stop and offer vault-init as a next step, not to launch straight into creating the folder skeleton without the user separately confirming they want it.
